key_insight: KANs are competitive aerodynamic surrogates for airfoil pressure prediction, but in this study they were slightly outperformed by a well-tuned MLP and outmatched by a GNN.
engineering_relevance: For fast surrogate modeling in aerodynamics, KANs offer a lower-complexity option with good interpolation across Mach number and angle of attack, which can support design and analysis workflows.
method: Compared KANs against MLPs and GNNs for predicting surface pressure distributions on subsonic and transonic airfoils.
Evaluated generalization over Mach number and angle of attack in a canonical fluid dynamics surrogate task.
Assessed model trade-offs in accuracy, complexity, and training time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KANs predict whole pressure-coefficient distributions well and interpolate across operating conditions, but their performance was marginally below MLPs and below GNNs, which achieved the best accuracy with longer training.
watch_item: KAN performance was highly sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and could suffer from training instabilities.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
